problem: Adobe sought recurring revenue and faster product updates.
title: Adobe shifts Creative Suite to the Creative Cloud subscription
context: Adobe moved its creative software from boxed perpetual licences toward a subscription.
decision_made: Make Creative Cloud subscriptions the main way to buy its creative tools.
observed_outcome: Creative Cloud subscriptions reached about 3.45 million by the end of fiscal 2014, up by over two million; recurring revenue rose to 66 percent of Q4 revenue from 44 percent a year earlier.
lessons: Subscription models can lift recurring revenue, but results depend on existing customer lock-in.
limitations: The 2013 announcement itself was not retrieved. Adobe had strong lock-in and brand, so results may not transfer to smaller companies. Customer dissatisfaction is not measured here.

claims.claim_text: Adobe moved its creative software toward Creative Cloud subscriptions.
Creative Cloud subscriptions grew by over two million to 3.454 million in fiscal 2014.
